transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Well, it’s nice to meet you too, Doctor. I, uh... I guess the main reason I finally made this appointment—and I've been putting it off for a while,
What has been bothering you the most lately?

I mean, what’s bothering me most is that I just can't keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. And it's not just the little things, it's the important stuff, the things I really need to get done for work. I’m a computer support specialist, right? So a lot of my job is figuring out why things aren't working. I'll get a ticket, a client's network is down or lagging or whatever, and I'll start tracing the problem. I pull up the logs, I'm looking at the data, I'm ready to figure it out. And then... I don't even know what happens. Ten minutes later, I realize I've just been staring at the screen. I'll have reread the exact same block of log entries, like, three times, and I still don't know what they actually say. It's like my brain just slides right off the information. I look at the words, the numbers, the IP addresses, and it's just noise. And then I have to start all over again, and by then I'm frustrated, and I'm worried the client is getting impatient, and... it's just exhausting. It takes me three times as long to do something that should be straightforward, just because I can't keep my focus locked in.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?
Worrying? Um... no, not really. Not about a lot of different things, anyway. I mean, obviously, I stress about the work stuff I just told you about,
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Down or depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, I get frustrated, like I was saying about the logs and the tickets and feeling like I'm letting people down because I can't just do the thing I'm supposed to do. That definitely gets me down in the moment, you know? It's discouraging when you know you're smart enough to do the job—I have a master's degree, for crying out loud, I know how networks operate—but your brain just won't cooperate. But it's not like a dark cloud hanging over my whole life, if that's what you mean. I still enjoy things when I'm not working, I still like hanging out with my friends, I still like tinkering with my own computers at home... well, when I can actually finish a project, anyway. But no, I don't wake up feeling sad or hopeless or anything like that. It's really just this constant, overwhelming frustration with myself and my inability to just focus. It's like my engine is running, but the transmission keeps slipping out of gear. So, depressed? No. Just incredibly, incredibly annoyed with my own brain.
Do you often feel very anxious when you have to interact with other people because you worry they might judge you?

Anxious about people judging me? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, I interact with people all day, right? As a support specialist, I'm constantly on the phone or on video calls with clients, or talking to the other techs on the floor. And honestly, I'm usually the one who knows what's going on—technically speaking, I mean. I know the systems inside and out. So when I'm talking to a client whose server just crashed, I'm not worried about them judging *me* as a person, you know? I'm just focused on the fact that I need to fix their problem. 

Sure, I get stressed if I'm taking too long because I kept losing my train of thought while checking their firewall configurations, but that's more about me being frustrated with myself, like I said before. It's not this deep-seated fear that they're looking at me and thinking I'm a weirdo or something. I actually like talking to people, for the most part. Sometimes I probably talk too much, to be honest. I'll get a client on the phone and start explaining the entire architecture of their network when all they wanted to know was why their email wasn't syncing. But no, I don't get that freezing, panicky feeling about being judged. I'm 53 years old, I've been doing this a long time, I know who I am. I just... I just wish my brain would stay on the track I put it on, instead of constantly derailing when I'm trying to work. But social anxiety? No, I wouldn't say I have that at all.
Did these concentration problems start after a major stress or life change?
